The Six Shuvüüsh Tribes: Masks, Terror-Birds, and the Next Ruler of the Steppe

Region (English scoring-table classification): Haless.

One-line positioning: Put on the ancestral masks, unite the steppe amid terror-bird cavalry and the Facestealer threat, then choose which great power to become.

Storytelling: High｜Mission-tree length: Short (10 shared clan missions, plus 7 Hus Bhal-specific missions)｜Mission-tree update: Base v1.37.5.0, updated by the 2026 regional diary｜Uniqueness: High｜Tedium: Medium-high｜Early pressure: Country-dependent; very high for Hus Bhal｜Expansion capacity: High.

Six countries, not one map colour

The scoring table's “Shuvüüsh Tribes” is a grouping. This compilation defines six 1444 candidates: Ashag Kuulgo V24, Hus Bhal V25, Zunk Kuulgo V26, Tsuista Khul Y90, Nuugdan Tsarai Y91, and Rüng Igedch Y92. All use the Shuvüüsh technology group in their history files and can therefore enter the same clan-specific mission set; they nevertheless have different primary cultures, positions, rulers, and opening relationships. Shared technology does not mean that all six countries are the same people, and it certainly does not mean that every Nuugdan Tsarai feature belongs to every tribe.【Local history script】【Local localisation】

The first three countries have Shuvüüsh primary culture; Tsuista Khul and Nuugdan Tsarai are Kuuldaar, while Rüng Igedch has its own culture. Hus Bhal starts under attack from Nuugdan Tsarai; Nuugdan Tsarai has the young female ruler Nurgai and exclusive events, and the other countries cannot automatically borrow her abilities.【Local history script】

Why everyone wears masks

The offline English Wiki records migration after the Day of Ashen Skies, the Three Brothers' mask tradition, and terror-bird riding as the shared history of this northern-Haless steppe. The old empire's unification, the 1081 assassination of the royal family, and the turmoil that followed explain why 1444 contains many competing tribes rather than one stable empire. Nuugdan Tsarai's rise is the history of one polity within that setting; it must not be written as though the other five countries had already sworn loyalty to it.【Wiki material】

Local narrative text gives the masks a more concrete purpose than “mysterious nomadic decoration”: Facestealers take faces and consume life and spirits, while ancestral masks provide protection. Dialogue even requires families to forget relatives already replaced by Facestealers, cutting off the power the monsters gain from memory. This brutal survival custom must be understood in the context of the monster threat; the simultaneous presence of ancestors, the dead, and masks is not by itself evidence that the country uses living souls as fuel.【Local narrative text】

The struggle against Facestealers also involves shamans, obsidian weapons, and incense. Together these systems connect religion, cavalry tactics, and spiritual warfare, making the unification of the steppe not only a matter of defeating other tribes but also of enabling the community to survive in a dangerous environment over the long term.

Ten shared missions, three great-power directions

The shared file defines 10 missions marked as generic, but their potential is restricted to the Shuvüüsh technology group; the accurate term is a “clan-specific shared tree”, not 10 independent unique missions for each country. The main line simultaneously calls for fighting Facestealers, winning clan support, unifying the steppe, restoring the homeland, and attacking the periphery. It also makes raiding records and neighbouring wealth objectives, so protection of the homeland and predatory raids coexist; it cannot be presented as only a heroic story of national unity.【Local script】【Local narrative text】

The final stretch can prepare the way toward Guwaamud Y96, Daxugo Y98, or Baztungh Khayus V28. These are conditional formable targets, not three buttons handed out indiscriminately after the shared missions. Guwaamud and Daxugo change the technology group and switch to non-generic missions on formation; the Baztungh Khayus formation effect read here did not show the same tree-switch instruction, so it must not be treated as equivalent. The larger campaigns after formation require renewed preparation in the new tree; the short shared tree must not create the false impression that the entire campaign is short.【Local script】

How to choose among the tribes

Hus Bhal is best for players who want a clearly independent branch: besides the shared tree, it has 7 unique missions dealing first with Nuugdan Tsarai and then with mountain residents, shrines, lakes, and the reconstruction of Khaantar. Its opening war pressure is verifiable fact and must not be treated as the same easy unification start as the other five countries.【Local script】

Nuugdan Tsarai suits players who prefer a strong central figure and an opening struggle for supremacy; its exclusive events centre on the Faceless Queen and her political legacy. No independent mission file described by the old document was found in the current version, so this article recognises only the shared tree and the locatable events. Tsuista Khul, Rüng Igedch, and the other two minor tribes are different geographic entrances into the same clan cycle; their independent historical material is sparse, so no complete dynasty or divergent end state is invented for them.

The two player posts cover only Nuugdan Tsarai and an older Daxugo campaign, and cannot establish the difficulty of the other five countries. The official regional diary provides design context for the masks and northern threat; the diary date remains unresolved, so its number is not used to claim a release date for each current mission.【Community opinion】【Related official development diary】

Personality and recommendation

Country v2.1 personality coordinates v2.1 values Reason to choose
Nuugdan Tsarai E96 · A88 · M/T92 I88 · P35 Neutral 47/100 · branch-dependent Shared-tree baseline; exclusive branch and evidence are in the body and its independent main JSON.
Hus Bhal E84 · A76 · M/T88 I85 · P55 Neutral 58/100 · branch-dependent Shared-tree baseline; exclusive branch and evidence are in the body and its independent main JSON.
Zunk Kuulgo E93 · A82 · M/T88 I82 · P38 Neutral 50/100 · branch-dependent Shared-tree baseline; evidence is in the body and its independent main JSON.
Tsuista Khul E93 · A82 · M/T88 I82 · P38 Neutral 50/100 · branch-dependent Shared-tree baseline; evidence is in the body and its independent main JSON.
Ashag Kuulgo E93 · A82 · M/T88 I82 · P38 Neutral 50/100 · branch-dependent Shared-tree baseline; evidence is in the body and its independent main JSON.
Rüng Igedch E93 · A82 · M/T88 I82 · P38 Neutral 50/100 · branch-dependent Shared-tree baseline; evidence is in the body and its independent main JSON.

The common route leans toward expansion, clan-leader authority, and ancestral magic. The four usual entrances are provisionally anchored at Neutral 50; Hus Bhal is Neutral 58 because of its verifiable protection and reconstruction branch; Nuugdan Tsarai is separately set to Neutral 47. These numbers describe the route, not six countries with identical personalities. The six independent result cards retain their own identities, pressures, and evidence confidence.

Protecting families, governing, and restoring the homeland are positive values; explicit raiding and terror-raiding objectives reduce restraint. War, nomadic culture, and mask religion are not penalised in themselves. The route suits players who enjoy terror-bird cavalry, ancestral religion, and rapid formation into a great power; players who dislike early wars, raiding objectives, or relearning a mission tree after formation should avoid it. Tag-specific conditions and evidence gaps are in the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in sequence as idea slots are filled, and the ambition applies after all seven are unlocked. Only national ideas are listed; racial, government, and mission rewards are not mixed into the values. Formation ideas are not automatically added to the old ideas. Idea descriptions may recall history or describe a future ideal; they do not automatically mean that the events had already happened in 1444.

Nuugdan Tsarai (Y91) — Nuugdan Tsarai Ideas

Traditions: Nuugdan Tsarai Traditions

Effects: Cavalry cost: -15%; Ruler's-faith advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Among the Kuuldaar

“Strange customs in these lands. They bury their dead like the Yan south of the misty hills instead of giving them a proper sky burial like Tsagaan taught our people. Here they fear not the facestealers. Many of the folk might’ve never encountered one in their lives, ever ignorant of what prowls further north.”

“They stray from Tsagaan’s wisdom.”

“Indeed my little one, they do. They, however, are not to be dismissed as complete fools. The way Tsagaan taught us served a purpose, specifically to combat the facestealing threat. If this threat is no longer present, the ritual can be potentially omitted. We have a lot to learn from the Kuuldaar in all aspects of life. Their art of the bow and its use from atop a terror-bird is a real sight to behold. I am old, but you and your cousins will be taught the way of the bow by our southern kinsmen. Their cultural ties to the Yan can prove useful for our clan, allowing our spies and informants to blend more easily in the south. Get used to these new traditions Nurgai. We may be here for a while”.

Effects: Global institution spread: +25%; Institution embracement cost: -20%.

Idea 2: Scourge of Yanshen

Nurgai stood in the Tsarai family tent with her two cousins, patiently listening to them discussing the clan’s next moves. It was rather unusual for someone outside the main branch to take part in these private deliberations, but Utalaai considered her more as a sister than a distant cousin. The sole survivour of the Bagaatun family, the former Kaasheg had adopted her in all but name.

“It’s been a decade since we’ve been pushed south by the treacherous scum, if we do not act swiftly we risk our clan being a footnote in the history of the Shuvüüshudi. We must pr-”

“Brother, excuse my interruption.The traitors have the momentum still; they claim legitimacy by donning the mask of the Old, despite being unworthy of even looking at it. If we want to succeed we need to first prove ourselves to the clans, gather them behind our banners. Yanshen is in turmoil and we must make the most out of our unfortunate relocation towards the border.”

After much deliberation, it was decided that revenge had to wait. There was opportunity in the south. The last question that needed to be answered was how to breach the border fortifications protecting the lower Yan.

“Zhiqian”, Nurgai uttered her first word of the evening. “I have a plan.”

Effects: Cavalry shock: +10%.

Idea 3: Leading By Example

When the Bhaatum returned from the first Shuvüüsh incursion into Yanshen in ages, the Kaasheg, Utalaai ak-Tsarai, did not return with it. Despite the joy of being successful in raiding all the way to the mouth of the Yan river and the eagerness to sort their loot, the clan had to proclaim a new leader.

The eldest of a well-respected family spoke first. “Utalaai’s children are still very young, leaving his brother, Khaaldak, as the only choice. He has proven himself time and time again.”

No one spoke back, only faint murmuring being heard among the various family heads present at the gathering, until Khaaldak himself stood up, the Tsarai mask firm in his hand. “Your words are wise elder, and I thank you for the nomination. However, there is someone far more deserving of the position. Someone with much more potential than me.”

Everyone knew who he meant. She had captured the fort of Xuanbik and led the Tsarai host all the way to the great city of Tianlou. Be it not for the unfortunate death of the Kaasheg, who knows what other machination she would have devised. No one argued against the proposal. The clan had a Kusheng for the first time, and soon, the entire Shuvüüshudi would follow her lead.

Effects: Prestige: +1; Female advisor chance: +50%.

Idea 4: The Spider's Web

“They are on the back foot, the Manticore Banner is flying over less and less Guwaduun settlements. The spirit lovers in the east have them retreating for the steppe.” Nurgai nodded for the faceless informant to continue on.

“The west is also in turmoil. The disparate Kuuldaar clans are all fighting between themselves for dominance, seeking to claim Ulaan’s mask from its shrine. The overseeing Death-Priest has vowed to not allow anyone to enter the shrine until the unnecessary bloodshed of our kin has ceased, however that might come to be.”

“What of the traitors?” The Kusheng’s voice toneless, with no emotion shown whatsoever, yet she was touching a subject most sensitive.

The informant took a few seconds to answer. “The Hus Bhaal have consolidated their control. They are actively sending envoys south, trying to find allies among the Kuuldar. It’s a short matter of time until Ashag Kuulgo also submits to them and the-”. Nurgai gestured to the informant to stop speaking, then stood up, the informant immediately doing the same. She exited the tent after a courtesy bow to the Kusheng. The next morning the bhaatum was mustered, ready to march north.

Effects: Diplomatic advisor cost: -25%.

Idea 5: Planning Ahead

After her unification of the steppe, everyone thought Nurgai would immediately march east and try to emulate Bhengudak’s conquest of the now fractured Dowon splinter states. She, however, knew that the Gowon were well prepared for her. The large mask-wearing Guwaadun population in the east served as the perfect cover for the Tsarai network of informants to operate in.

The armies of the Gowon alliance stayed levied at the border for months waiting for the seemingly inevitable invasion of the newly ascended Queen. Instead, a lone messenger arrived on his terror-bird. When the Shuvüüsh conducted diplomacy, they would arrive mounted on their terror-birds if the message was that of war. The alliance feared the worst, but were slightly relieved when they read the proposal.

“The steppe has been pacified and the Kaashegate has no intention to cross into Gowon. You are relieved of your duty protecting the old Daengun territories in Yanshen, for the Great Kusheng shall take on this mantle. In exchange for delivering you this tranquility, we ask for access to Bhengudak’s great temple and his mask.” It was not so much a proposal as a threat. The Gowon silence was interpreted as a form of silent acceptance.

Effects: Ruler administrative skill: +1.

Idea 6: Forming a Legend

It has been decades since that fateful day. The day she felt she was destined for greatness, her arrow as if guided by the Shepherd themselves. Raising Altan’s mask from the pretender’s lifeless body, she had no desire to wear it. It would be an easy way to cement her legitimacy but Nurgai had vowed to unify the Shuvüüsh by merit and merit alone. She returned the mask to its shrine in Zougzengom, making sure that all could see her never wearing it. She had even refused the Tsarai clan’s mask when she was proclaimed Kusheng, even allowing her cousin to wear it instead, an act of defiance that almost cost her legitimacy in her people’s eyes.

Now she stood here, at the royal palace of Damaogong, having led the Shuvüüsh to what is arguably their greatest achievement. Her wisdom and might considered by all to be unmatched, despite seemingly never having communed with any of the great ancestors. But they were wrong on one account; after unifying the Shuvüüsh, she had secretly travelled to Bhengudak’s temple and briefly wore the mask by revealing her identity to the overseeing Death-Priest.

“Our purpose is to guide the Saanorgegh faithful until the day the masks will be broken and we return to the Supreme Spirit. You, Nurgai, have no need of our guidance. Forge your own legend.”

Effects: Core-creation cost: -10%.

Idea 7: The Faceless Queen

Throughout her reign, Nurgai Bagaatun kept breaking tradition after tradition of Shuvüüsh rulers. Early in her life she had shown fascination with the Luzhong empire’s wonders in the southern steppe, keenly studying the ruins of their once great fortifications, a curiosity quite uncharacteristic. The first major tradition she broke, was it by intended scheming or sheer circumstance and merit, was her ascension to the head of the Tsarai clan in lieu of her cousin. No one reacted. The refusal to wear the Tsarai mask followed and still, no one reacted. Maybe she had greater ambitions, they thought. The greatest act of defiance though, was the refusal to wear Altan’s mask after reclaiming it. No one reacted, maybe she wanted to first wear another great mask, they thought. Then, she refused to wear any of the great masks, much to the surprise of everyone. No one reacted still. It was too late for that; Nurgai had won the steppe, and with it she had won the respect of all her kin.

After her death following her conquests in Yanshen, Nurgai’s soul was bound to the mask she wore her entire lifetime. While she ruled Khaantar and Yan alike, everyone from the smallfolk to the Yomod Rush and even the eunuchs of Yanshen felt close to Nurgai, as if the nation’s ruler was one of them. Maybe it was the mask. The blank, unadorned, bone-white mask, worn by The Faceless Queen.

Effects: Missionary strength: +2%.

Ambition: Nuugdan Tsarai Ambition

Effects: Province warscore cost: -10%.

Guwaamud (Y96) — Guwaamud Ideas

Traditions: Guwaamud Traditions

Effects: Years of separatism: -10; Trade steering: +20%.

Idea 1: Guwaaduni Irredentism

We stand at a crossroads. We have revived Bhengudak’s empire, but there is still work to be done. We may have claimed the mantle, but there is still kin of ours, both east and west, that lives outside the great empire’s borders.Some of them even looking down upon us, the Gowon considering us half-bred barbarians and the Khantaar dismissing us as sedentarized and weak. These affronts have to be rectified. All the Shuvüüsh and every last Gowon must come under the empire’s protection, for that is the only way for peace.

Effects: Liberty desire from subject development: -0.25.

Idea 2: The Great Khaashegate

Bhengudak was the one to unify the Shuvüüsh after centuries of loose confederations of clans and tribes wandering the vast steppe. He was the one to bring the three great Izhuun to heel and subjugate the disparate Bhaatum. He was the one to lead them into Dowon and lay claim to the fertile lands in the east. He was the one to reestablish the Great Kaashegate, and it is we that have achieved this noble goal once more. All of that was done through blood and steel, few ever bowed without the need of violence. The battlefield is where we won our empire, and the battlefield seems to be the only place where we can win it back.

Effects: Army morale: +15%.

Idea 3: Bhengudak’s Legacy

Bhengudak Izhuun Ak-Tsagaan is our prodigal ancestor and the first person to be deemed worthy by the priesthood to have his soul bound to a unique mask along with the Three Brothers of Yore. His legacy is the pride of our noble clan but it is also a curse. Bhengudak’s achievements cast a colossal shadow that our rulers will have to try very hard to escape from, let alone leave their own marks in history. His great mask is the one favoured by the Kaasheg. In a twisted bittersweet way, Bhengudak is still active in the rule of the empire he established, bound by mystic ritual to provide guidance to Guwaamuud until his great mask is shattered and his soul returned to the Supreme Spirit.

Effects: Monthly splendor: +1; Reform progress growth: +15%.

Idea 4: Between Worlds

Our realm stands at a crossroads between civilizations. Civilizations that have little relation to one another, the diametrically different conditions they were forged in driving them further and further away from one another. To the north, the hardy Khudi, living in a harsh climate with few resources to sustain big populations, constantly trying to survive against nature and spirit alike. To the south, the opulent Yan, satisfying their hubris with grand constructions whenever they aren’t toiling under the boot of some tyrant or dying in some pointless war.

Even in our own realm, the rich cities of the Gowon in the east have nothing in common with the moving settlements of the Shuvüüsh. We must make the most out of this inherent diversity, however difficult managing the needs of people so different in nature might be.

Effects: army_tradition_decay：-0.01; Development cost: -5%.

Idea 5: Neokttareum Syncretism

Bhengudak ruled both as Kaasheg and Ambahoron. The Gowon accepted him as their Sage-King, anointed such in Nakeseom by Sado, a fragment of Huszieng the great fox spirit herself, allowing him to enforce his rule and decrees on the Spirit inhabitants of the realm. This syncretism was maintained through a delicate balance that relied on both our religions fundamentally not being at odds with each other cosmologically, despite our death-priests making most spirits nervous with their mere presence. The spirit-lovers, as some of the more radical Saanorgegh faithful called their eastern neighbours, were not only tolerated, but fully accepted and allowed to practice their local religious traditions and customs.

Effects: Heretic tolerance: +2.

Idea 6: Prosperity for All

At Guwaamuud’s height, trade was flowing freely in the eastern sea. From the very far away lands of the Triunics, to the southernmost Halessi corners of Binhrung and Arawkelin, traders could be spotted traversing the Gowon ports, peddling their wares and buying ours to bring back to their distant homelands. The nomadic Shuvüüsh could not be fully controlled at all times, and thus raids into Yanshen were not an uncommon occurrence to say the least, however none of these transgressions were sanctioned by the official government in Onman. Despite this official policy of peace, maritime trade was the preferred method of commerce for all foreigners, save the occasional Rünsukhi peddler or Rukunai delegation crossing the steppe to engage in trade.

Effects: Construction cost: -15%.

Idea 7: Spirit Auxiliaries

While the old empire succeeded in balancing the Shuvüüsh and the Gowon, they were always wary of their Gowon subjects’ loyalty to the state. These suspicions were not fully unwarranted of course, as the Gowon needed time to accept the terror-bird riders as their rulers. Thus, the old empire’s military was mostly composed of Shuvüüsh warriors, divided in 5 Uvaadum with a very small number of Gowon serving mainly in non-combat roles. Now that our hold over the east has been solidified and the Spirits of these lands have started to accept our rule more eagerly, it is time to also reorganize our military ranks. The populous Gowon should serve mainly as infantry while the Spirits willing to fight can be assigned the role of elite shock troops. While we may lack the ability to field entire spirit armies as the ancient Sage-Kings did, we can still use them, especially in Yanshen, where many times our enemies lack ways to efficiently deal with them.

Effects: Shock damage: +10%.

Ambition: Guwaamud Ambition

Effects: Force limit contribution from subjects: +100%.

Daxugo (Y98) — Great Daxugo Ideas

Traditions: Daxug Traditions

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +20%; Advisor cost: -15%.

Idea 1: What Is Daxugo

At first, the Yanshen saw us only as Shuvüüsh invaders, while we called ourselves Daxugo—the Great Empire, believing we were destined to restore order. As we learned their language and script and governed their towns, the Yanshen gradually accepted that Daxugo had taken root in their land. With the signing of the Tianlou Concord between ourselves and the Yanshen states—standing together against external foes and growing ever more intertwined—we ceased to be clearly distinguished from one another: you within us, and us within you.

Yet our ancestral beliefs and customs endured, so that even as we came to be regarded as Yanshen, we retained a distinct character of our own. Over generations, a new identity emerged:

We are Yanshen, and we are the Empire.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Idea 2: Land of Many

The soul-farms of the Northern Plains were once regarded as lands where spirits settled more firmly than men. Through the stewardship of successive monarchs and the adoption of Yanshen techniques, these lands have been transformed into fertile fields. Their steady abundance of grain has rooted the people to the soil, replacing wandering with permanence and allowing communities to flourish in stability.

Along the Yanhe, authority restored order; refugees returned in great numbers, merchants gathered once more, and revived river trade bound the region together as towns prospered again.

One land feeds the people, the other gathers them — farmland and markets reinforcing one another, driving Daxugo’s population to unprecedented heights and swelling its armies as never before.

Under our rule, this land has truly become a Land of the Many.

Effects: Land force limit modifier: +20%; global_manpower_modifier：+10%.

Idea 3: Imperial Spears and the Yanshen Corps

As Daxugo’s ties with Yanshen grew ever closer, its military entered a period of transition. The Shuvüüsh elite — the Imperial Spears — upheld the traditional terror-bird shock cavalry doctrine, while the emerging Yanshen Corps advocated integrating terror-birds into disciplined infantry formations.

The clash of these military doctrines reflected the tensions of cultural fusion and gradually reshaped the army. The Imperial Spears began experimenting with applying Yanshen systems of discipline and the use of artillery to terror-bird units, while supporters of Yanshen corps theory increasingly incorporated the terror-birds’ devastating flanking charges into large-scale formations. At the same time, they sought to exploit the terror-birds’ formidable carrying capacity to establish reliable supply lines. Through mutual exchange and adaptation, both sides absorbed the strengths of the other’s doctrine, forging a new path between steppe ferocity and Yanshen order.

Effects: Army drill: +5%.

Idea 4: The Transformation of the Eunuchs

When our tribes first entered Yanshen, the Faceless Queen was compelled to incorporate the eunuchs into the imperial administration in order to stabilize the realm and ease the burdens of governance. Yet as their influence steadily expanded and they began to encroach upon royal authority, restraining their power became the enduring objective of successive monarchs. Several emperors sought to curb the eunuchs’ dominance—some by elevating decorated Daxugo nobles to court positions as a counterweight, others by establishing a new corps of officials selected independently of the eunuch system to assume their responsibilities. These efforts were not without bloodshed, and palace purges were far from rare.

After a long era of reform, as key state institutions gradually came under the control of the nobility and Daxugo officials chosen through the examination system, the eunuchs were stripped of most of their political authority and redirected toward scholarship, record-keeping, and the arts. With the continued advance of imperial centralization, their influence steadily waned.

Effects: Technology cost: -5%; Idea cost: -5%.

Idea 5: Fanwang

In the Empire’s early days, when Daxugo had only just transformed from tribes into a monarchy, it struggled to control its distant frontiers. Though Yanshen eunuchs were brought into the administration, the monarch refused to entrust them with full authority. Instead, remote regions were granted to cadet royals or cooperative warlords, giving them the right to raise troops, levy taxes, and maintain their own officials. In return, they were to guard the borders, send regular tribute, and answer imperial calls to war.

Over time, however, these fanwang lords built their own power bases. Some delayed tribute, ignored summons, or forged quiet ties with foreign powers. Far from the capital and commanding their own armies, they shifted from frontier shields to potential threats.

Rumors of conspiracy reached the capital, forcing the monarch to ask:

Should these border realms be entrusted to more reliable hands?

Effects: Administrative efficiency: +5%.

Idea 6: Rite of Following Heaven

Daxugo’s state rites blend the ancient Shuvüüsh mask tradition with the ceremonial order of Yanshen. After fasting, the emperor ascends the altar wearing an unadorned white mask, signifying that he stands beyond any single clan as the ritual bearer of the empire’s shared order, offering sacrifice to Heaven.

The High Priest dons the black mask of the Shepherd of Souls and, amid music and the threefold offering, calls upon the ancestral spirits of the Three Brothers—Tsagaan, Ulaan, and Altan—to watch over the rite; the masks of other honored ancestors are arranged beside him as witnesses to the ceremony.

Terror-birds, revered as sacred beasts and symbols of virtue, take part in the ceremony and lead the ritual procession; their hatchlings are bestowed upon meritorious servants according to Yanshen court tradition.

Through this union of steppe mask-law and Yanshen ceremonial order, Daxugo establishes a unified state rite across its vast domains, affirming its rightful rule and its duty to safeguard all lives within its realm.

Effects: True faith tolerance: +2.

Idea 7: Daxugo-style Diplomacy

As Daxugo developed and the surrounding situation evolved, the Empire gradually formed a distinctive diplomatic corps. Unlike settled states that relied on permanent embassies, Daxugo stood between the steppe and the prosperous cities of Yanshen; facing diverse states and circumstances, its envoys evolved into a mobile, composite diplomatic force combining ritualized contractual practices, negotiation, and liaison functions.

These itinerant missions moved between courts, tribal encampments, and commercial cities, handling treaty communication and mediating border frictions. Their experience, forged amid conflicts among the steppe tribes, allowed them to buffer disputes before tensions among concord members escalated, ensuring the continued operation of the defense-oriented Tianlou Concord. By linking networks of relations and trade across the steppe and Yanshen, they also provided concord members with tangible benefits beyond security, exerting lasting influence within the concord framework.

Effects: Diplomats: +1; Improve relations: +10%.

Ambition: Daxug Ambition

Effects: Administrative capacity modifier: +15%.

Baztungh Khayus (V28) — Baztung Khayus Ideas

Traditions: Baztung Khayus Traditions

Effects: global_manpower_modifier：+20%; Ruler administrative skill: +1.

Idea 1: A River In Dry Land

Khaantar is a desert wasteland that knows little of mercy, but it is not without boons if one knows where to look. A cave that holds respite; a small river giving bountiful water and pasture; even the very ruins themselves can house a small army in the shade, if needed. Yet there is more to these ruins than just the things needed to live.

Indeed, there are relics within that we can use to thrive. We send parties across these ruins to strip them bare, and to bring them back for study, whether for personal use or for other pursuits such as adorning the rooms of the greatest of us. Some of the Runsukhi and Rukunai have an inkling of what such relics might be used for, and thus are routinely conscripted for these efforts.

The desert houses secrets that the greatest of the Khaantari, the greatest of us, will use to truly thrive in what once was.

Effects: Land attrition: -15%.

Idea 2: Wear The Self

A mask was a shield to us, a symbol of our heritage and a way to honor our ancestors who have discovered the secrets to ward off the Facestealers. But now that we have achieved so much more than them, is it really so appropriate to wear the mask of just a faceless person, or of these ancestors?

Our masks have grown since our days of warlordship. Now we have become Baztungh Khayus; we have outgrown our need to be a copy, faceless in a crowd, easily forgotten upon death or upon being consumed by Facestealers. Now we can truly express ourselves in a way that represents the core being of ourselves. Gold to go with triumph, red to match honor – a blue fractal pattern to represent endless wisdom. We have grown to wear a new persona for ourselves, and there will be no need to go back to how we were.

Effects: Province warscore cost: -15%.

Idea 3: Mass Terror

Glimpse a single terrorbird rider, and know that there are far more on all sides ready to slip in and gut you. You are already dead - they will have set up days beforehand, half a day’s distance to the left of you and to the right – if possible, even half a day behind you. They will wait and wait and wait until the signal is given, just as the eggs of the terrorbirds themselves wait for the right conditions to hatch.

The terrorbird riders are terrifying to behold, the Yomod Rush having perfected the breeding of them to ensure their speed, survivability and intelligence in all conditions under the guidance of a rider. Though there have been some grumblings about the demands of expanding the breeding programs, they still abide by our rule and foresight. Just enough to ensure mass destruction, just enough to ensure the tactics used work as intended.

These are the tactics that evolved from the simple days of warlordism, back when the Baztungh Khayus was just a simple band. Now? Now they ride, and when they ride they leave nothing behind.

Effects: Cavalry combat ability: +25%.

Idea 4: First Among Brothers

Those who boast no ancestry in ancient Khaantar are fit only to be tributaries, outsiders with claim to only a fraction of the greatness and protection of the Shuvuushi and Kuuldar.

There is a more fraternal affection of sorts to those that do share that Khaantari heritage. The Runsukhi and Rukunai, those who either stayed within the wastes that once made home or retreated to the plateaus up high, are ultimately our brothers. Some might claim hold truer to Khaantari wisdom than the Shuuvushi, that they should guide the brethren – in this they are mistaken. It was the Shuuvushi and Kuuldar who united all of us, after all. Where our brothers only fought to survive, we fought to thrive. Therefore, it is we who will guide them to greatness, who will stamp down on foolish practices and help them don the masks which protect and represent… whether they want us to or not.

Still, they are treated better than the outsiders, still higher on the hierarchy than them. However, if an outsider were to prove themselves, then perhaps they too might be said to have the blood of Khaantar in their veins?

Effects: Ruler's-culture advisor cost: -20%.

Idea 5: You'll Never See It Coming

The greatest challenge for a conquering army is information control: that which one gains for oneself, and that which one’s enemy gains. Scouts, watch-towers, and spies are the bane of any army that has to march through hostile lands to reach the fight; traps and poisons are set, lands are burned, any possible means taken to delay progress and cause losses of manpower and material.

But what if you were fast enough? What if you targeted areas where scouts would naturally be placed, to run them down before they could bring back information? What if you quietly suborned the watchtowers? Ensured that no news, no information ever reached the enemy armies, save a terrifying swell of silence? Then, indeed, the enemies would never know you were there, or at least not your true numbers, until it was too late. They would never see it coming.

Effects: Movement speed: +15%; Cavalry to infantry ratio: +25%.

Idea 6: Innocent Sin

Khaantar was not perfect. They fell, after all, to the teeming hordes of Facestealers and the fall of the land around them. Yet can we truly consider them culpable? How can one truly prepare, truly survive such conditions without splintering, without cracking?

We have the answer. Our ways, perfected over millennia of war. Our roots, torn and adrift amongst the terror birds. Our strength, bound by the rule of our great leaders. Our bonds through kin, our masks, our everything. We have brought order back to Khaantar. And Khaantar shall return, not as the empire that died through ruin, but as an empire that thrives in even the toughest conditions. Decrees shall be made: Khaantar shall be mapped out, with the Runsukhi giving over the finest pastures for the greatest of us. No longer shall we be purely settled; we shall be as we were, true Shuvvushi warlords. No longer will the Rukunai hoard secrets: all will be spilled like entrails from a beast. No longer shall there be any dissent: they will understand that only we can truly guide Khaantar’s beating heart back into place.

This innocent sin will be rectified.

Effects: Reform progress growth: +15%.

Idea 7: End It Thus

Beneath the ruins, nestled into the foot of the four peaks, lies a staff of gleaming purple imbued with powerful spiritual energy. The area is bereft of Facestealers, of horrors, of spirits. It is obvious to us after using it upon a roving Facestealer that it dispels them back wherever they once arose out of; we watch them briefly glow with energy before disappearing utterly.

We shall find where they live, where their cavern of origin lies. We shall use this relic on them, and we shall tear the Facestealers asunder. We will end it thus!

Effects: National unrest: -2.

Ambition: Baztung Khayus Ambition

Effects: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Hus Bhal (V25) — Hus Bhal Ideas

Traditions: Hus Bhal Traditions

Effect: Cavalry cost: -15%; same-religion advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Life in the Saddle

The Shuvüüsh inhabit a harsh land, a land where few things thrive. Deserts stretching for miles and miles, with the scarce vegetation clinging to the few pockets of water that are found in this desolate land. Any wildlife managing to survive in the destitution of the Shuvüüshudi is also seldom encountered, preferring to remain outside one’s gaze. The saving grace for our people is the symbiotic relationship with the creatures known as terror-birds. Our clan’s historical position on the northwestern fringes of the steppe necessitates that we are constantly on the move on top of our trusted bestial companions.

Effect: Envoy travel time: -30%.

Idea 2: Adjudicators of the Steppe

The Shuvüüsh are the only people, probably the only surviving creatures, who can stand in front of a Facestealer and live to tell the tale. Even more so, the Hus Bhal serves as the steppe vanguard against this otherworldly threat. We boast the greatest amount of black masked death-priests and a disproportionately small number of white masked Shamans relative to our southern and eastern kin. Our few white masked Shamans take the mantle of Adjudicators, judging spirits and allowing or forbidding them to cross southwards.

Effect: Tolerance of the true faith: +2.

Idea 3: Trail of Sustenance

The terror-birds are arguably our people’s greatest asset. They allow us to survive in the harsh conditions of what we call home, while they also enable us to be feared and respected by outsiders. These creatures’ lifecycle and general needs are very specific and require their constant movement between the frozen pastures in the north during winter and the southern warmer lands in the south during summer. This trip has to be made yearly by the Yomod Rüsh of all the clans. Our position along this route gives us a strong hand in all matters diplomatic and mercantile.

Effect: Province trade power modifier: +10%.

Idea 4: Dakilbege Nuk

The forsaken lake serves as a landmark in the vast emptiness of the steppe, the largest body of water one will stumble upon while traversing this barren land. As such, the lake serves as an anchor for the chi-starved spirits that roam our lands. The Dakil Huu, the lake’s spirit provides protection to any wandering spirit that had the fortune of escaping the clutches of the facestealing ones.

Effect: Army attrition: -10%.

Idea 5: Altan’s Guidance

Altan the Old was the eldest of the three brothers, leading our people during the Huusing as they fled from the west. While his brothers excelled in wisdom and might each, his distinctive aptitude towards gouvernance and decision-making is what gave him the role of our ancestors’ leader during their most troubling time, ensuring that they do not fall to infighting and petty squabbles between themselves. His insight still guides us in our struggle to reunify our kin.

In his honour, a shrine was erected in Zougzengom in the years following his death. Typical to Shuvüüsh style, the shrine is no bigger than a family tent in size. Built from consecrated wood and adorned by carvings depicting various nature scenes, the shrine is situated at one of the few oasis that dot the western steppe, with the surrounding low vegetation perfectly complementing the calm and collected aura that the shrine exhibits. His mask, when not worn by our Izhuun, is proudly sitting at its shrine in Zougzengom, far away from prying hands.

Effect: All estates' loyalty equilibrium: +5%.

Idea 6: Heart of the Khantaar

Our traditional grazing pastures lie at the heart of the Khantaari people’s homeland; if you can call home the lands we and our distant kin inhabit. The great door of Haakukulga reminds us of the tenacity and isolation of our western kin while the vast steppe that lies beyond makes sure we never forget the lands we wandered since our birth. Be it a period of peace or hostility with our southern and western kin, we are well accustomed with their traditions and know well how to conduct diplomacy in both the tents of the Shuvüüsh and the monasteries of the Rukunai.

Effect: Improve relations: +20%.

Idea 7: Lessons of the Past

After the royal family’s untimely demise and the collapse of the Great Kaashegate in 1081, The until-then minor clan of Nuugdan Tsarai seized the mask of Altan the Old from its resting space, seemingly breaking all tradition by their Izhuun wearing the mask. Little did everyone know, the Kaasheg was already dead and thus no tradition was dishonoured, no unwritten law was broken. The Tsarai had planned ahead their moves and were sure the emperor laid dead at the royal palace. They would go on to lose control of the northern steppe and most importantly Zougzengom to the Oinukhudi Empire in a century’s time.

However, we had learned a lot from the Tsarai gambit all these years ago. When the Oinukhudi weaknesses became apparent in the 13th century and the state fell into civil strife, our clan was ready. We seized the opportunity and declared the independence of the steppe, with most minor clans rallying behind the Hus Bhaal banners. Our legitimacy to rule was sealed when our Izhuun donned Altan’s mask after a sizable chunk of the Tsarai clan’s subjects recognized our right to rule and offered it to us as a token of their subordination to our great clan.

Effect: Global spy defence: +20%; Harsh treatment cost: -25%.

Ambition: Hus Bhal Ambition

Effect: Province warscore cost: -10%.

Zunk Kuulgo (V26) — Zunk Kuulgo Ideas

Traditions: Zunk Kuulgo Traditions

Effect: Cavalry cost: -15%; same-religion advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Spirit Rights

While it is not unheard of for spirits to maintain amicable relations with the Shuvüüsh, it is certainly not the norm in the northern parts of the steppe. While our southern Kuuldaar cousins are more open to communication and cohabitation with spirits, this is not the case further north. However, despite the general detest most spirits have for the Shuvüüsh, the Zunk Kuulgo can proudly say that they are one of the very few clans who have worked to dispel this notion. While our shamans maintain the power to dissipate a spirit’s chi, we make sure they respect their rights and that they are kept on a tight leash so that no misunderstanding may happen. Spirits roam somewhat carefree in lands under the clan’s control, having assurances from the Izhuun that their rights will be respected.

Effect: National unrest: -2.

Idea 2: Quality over Quantity

Our clan has the lowest number of terror-birds among our peers in Shuvüüshudi. Our position in its easternmost edge places us far away from the warm southern lands where the Great Hatching takes place and a good distance from the freezing grazing grounds to the north that are ideal for terror-bird herding. Hence, our few Yomod Rüsh families take pride in the Terror-Birds they raise, paying much more attention to each and every individual creature, resulting in a better quality of steeds relative to our neighbours.

Effect: Cavalry flanking ability: +50%.

Idea 3: Crossroads of Civilizations

Our Clan occupies a piece of land right at the point when Yan, Khantaar, and Gowon cultures meet. While we are definitely part of the greater Shuvüüsh culture, we undeniably exhibit characteristics of our neighbours to a greater extent than the rest of the Shuvüüsh. We do partake in Zhuong and terror-bird races as do all of our kinsmen but we also burn our dead like our immediate Yan neighbours. We adhere to the Saanorgegh faith but we respect Spirit-Law and maintain good relations with the few spirits that may end up in our corner of the world.

Effect: Number of accepted cultures: +2.

Idea 4: Mediators of the Steppe

The Zunk Kuulgo, the clan of the eastern gate, always served a niche role in the inter political struggles of the steppe. Be it united or fragmented, the steppe always turned to our clan for mediation in matters between clans. Famed for the wisdom of its Izhuuns throughout the years, their souls still advising the reigning Izhuun, the clan has successfully brokered peace, negotiated artifact returns, and facilitated alliances time and time again throughout the years.

Effect: Prestige: +1.

Idea 5: Ties to the East

While never having been fully trusted by the Gowon to the east, the eastern gate clan has always enjoyed a better relationship with the various Gowon kingdoms than the rest of the Shuvüüsh. Situated at the Yan border near Jiantsiang, the clan’s hostility usually turned towards the southern Yan states, striking at every opportune moment. This along with the long-lasting rivalry with the neighbouring Ashag Kuulgo left the clan’s hands tied and seeking closer ties with the Gowon kingdoms.

Effect: Improve relations: +20%.

Idea 6: Opportunistic Diplomacy

Unable to muster the numbers of the southern clans and having no access to the rich Guwaadun cities of the northeast, the Zunk Kuulgo have always employed cunning diplomacy and opportunism to survive. Internal strife to the south meant that the clan would focus its military endeavours towards the Yan. Civil war in the east meant that they would offer their military services to whichever side they thought was going to win. Unfortunately, this very necessity for opportunism meant that at times of a unified Gowon state, Zunk Kuulgo would find themselves subordinate to that very state they seeked to diplomatically exploit.

Effect: Diplomatic relations: +1.

Idea 7: Kadash Ak-Zunk

The clan’s famed progenitor, Kadash Ak-Zunk, was according to legend a member of Bhengudak’s inner circle and rumoured to have also been his nephew. He is attested following Bhengudak south in his unification of the Shuvüüsh and was later tasked with leading the host that would later develop into the 2nd Uvaadum into southern Gowon. An exemplary tactician and shrewd diplomat, he commanded the respect of his peers and played a vital part in the nobility’s right to carve their own clan-masks. He was one of the first clan heads to be bound onto a mask, his original mask serving as the ak-Zunk clan head’s mask even to this day.

Effect: Army leader shock: +1.

Ambition: Zunk Kuulgo Ambition

Effect: Province warscore cost: -10%.

Tsuista Khul (Y90) — Tsuista Khul Ideas

Traditions: Tsuista Khul Traditions

Effect: Cavalry cost: -15%; same-religion advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Summer Hatching Grounds

The terror-bird is a peculiar creature, its lifecycle unique and intricate in nature, it needs extensive care from its nativity in the egg until well into its adulthood. Part of this lifecycle is the Daiqi Huur, the great bonfire. During the summer months, the Yomod Rüsh families of the entire steppe make the journey south to hatch their eggs in this grand display of mutual respect among the Shuvüüsh. The fire can burn from days to weeks and with a clear sky the smoke can be even seen from the High Temple in Jiangtsiang, reminding the southerners and their Tiger lords that their walls will not hold forever.

Effect: Tribes Loyalty Equilibrium: +10%.

Idea 2: The Incorruptible

Our lands stand at one end of the Demon Hills. What is usually referred to as the “other” side by the Oni, and for good reason. Despite the Oni finding success in corrupting and infiltrating with their vile magic the lands to the west and south of the hills, they are unlikely to ever make such incursions into our lands. We may share our southern cousins’ love for tea, but we certainly do not share their aversion towards the dark arts. Instead, they are content with raiding attempts on our fabled Spirit-Farms.

The Spirit farms situated closer to the borders are guarded night and day by the Incorruptible, warriors chosen by our most wise Death-Priests that have undertaken extensive mental and physical training. Equipped with Blessed Ebony Blades and Arrows, they are some of the few in all of Haless that can claim to match the Shirgrii monks in single combat.

After serving their tenure in this prestigious yet demanding post, the Incorruptible are put at the heads of hosts to act as generals and advisors, taking advantage of their exposure to the various unique and often unorthodox military tactics of the Oni.

Effect: Yearly corruption: -0.1.

Idea 3: Ulaan's Might

Ulaan the Fierce was the youngest of the three brothers and the mightiest warrior amongst them. As the legend goes, his actions constantly towed the line between boldness and rashness. His elder brothers’ guidance was often necessary to ensure he did not act in haste or retaliate when not absolutely necessary.

However, this inherent spur to action that he exhibited is said to have saved our ancestors more than once during the Husuusing. Ever eager to lead from the front, Ulaan’s bold personality and stalwart sense of duty is what guides our clan up to this very day. His mask, when not chosen by the current Izhuun, sits at a tightly guarded shrine in Dhashujuj, constantly under the auspice of the most senior Death-Priest amongst the Tuiista Khul.

Effect: Shock damage received: -10%.

Idea 4: Kuuldaari Archers

The Kuuldaari are a hybridized people. The large (large by Shuvüüshudi standards) number of proto-Beikling people that lived in what is today the southernmost part of the terror-bird riders’ domain, were gradually assimilated in the Shuvüüsh style of life. Although not as nomadic in nature as their northern brothers, the Kuuldaari are still ferocious riders and there is a substantial amount of Yomod Rüsh families amongst them.

On top of the many Beikling cultural traditions, the Kuuldaari have also inherited the art of archery. Instead of practicing the traditional Shuvüüsh jousting called Zoungh, the Kuuldaari prefer to challenge each other to horseback shooting contests. A Kuuldaari regiment of masked riders with their bows have routed Yan armies ten times their size more times than any scholar of Yingchen would like to admit.

Effect: Infantry fire: +10%.

Idea 5: The Spirit-Farms

Coexistence with Spirits is the status quo in southern Gozengun. The Shuvüüsh way of handling spirits might be unconventional by any other standards, but for us it is the way we have been taught by the Shepherd of Souls. Our Death-Priests claim the right to exorcise any spirit they deem unworthy. However, we do recognize that there are many spirits who are not only harmless to us, but one would say rather beneficial.

The Spirit population in the south of the steppe is larger than its human counterpart. These Spirits congregate on what are known as Spirit-Farms, where they cultivate the land. Our warriors protect them from Oni eyeing their chi and our Death-Priests make sure no rogue Facestealer find their way that far south. So, they endlessly, tirelessly toil the land, providing terror-bird and man with sustenance for the harsh life in the steppe.

Effect: Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 6: Reaching the River

In 1444 our Izhuun Ulqilir ak-Khul, consulting with the mask of Ulaan the Fierce proposed to the great Faceless Queen a deal that she in her infinite wisdom deemed fit to accept. “We want to reach the Yan River”. Those were the final words he uttered before the Queen after explaining in detail his desire to cross the Tuiista Khul into Yanshen proper and settle the Jinqiu valley.

The Queen, having grown up amongst the Kuuldaar knew of their worth and martial prowess and accepted the deal, being sure that the Kuuldaari terror-riders, although few in number, could wreak havoc in the plains of Upper Yanshen unopposed. “The Kaashegate will aid the Khul in breaking through the hills of the Beikling. In exchange, the southern steppe and the Spirit Farms would come under direct control of the Kaasheg. Furthermore, the great Khul’s terror-bird archers should answer the Kaasheg’s call should the need arise”. The Izhuun raised his cup of spirit-wine and nodded in agreement. At that moment, the Yan’s fate was sealed.

Effect: Raze power gain: +0.2.

Idea 7: Strangers in a Strange Land

The southern invasion was driven, fundamentally, by a desire to find a better life. The Kuuldaari riders who were set on their nomadic ways remained with the Kaashegate while many of the Tuiista families were settled into the hills and valleys of their Beikling cousins. They started wearing their masks less and less. Here, in the south, far from the threat of facestealing monstrosities the masks started to fill a strictly cultural role, much like the Beikling tradition of wearing enchanted masks. With time, only the house heads wore the faceless masks, while more and more individuals started to opt for traditional burials instead of being inducted into the heirloom masks.

Sky burials were already getting less and less popular among the Kuuldaari, with earthly entombment being preferred even before our invasion of Yanshen. In a few short centuries, the only remnant of the old Kuuldaari way of life would be the powerful Death-Priests still donning their pitch black masks, ever vigilant on their duties.

Effect: Promote culture cost: -20%.

Ambition: Tsuista Khul Ambition

Effect: Province warscore cost: -10%.

Ashag Kuulgo (V24) — Ashag Kuulgo Ideas

Traditions: Ashag Kuulgo Traditions

Effect: Cavalry cost: -15%; same-religion advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Martial Minds of the Steppe

While treated as lesser by the other clans, the Ashag Kuulgo maintain their descent from the Three Brothers in the same manner that all the other Izhuun do. While not boasting their kin’s achievements at a superficial glance, given a better look into Shuvüüsh history one might be surprised by the impact the Ashag Kuulgo had in the exploits of the Shuvüüsh people time and time again. From Baohu to Encehen ak-Ashag, the Bhaatum has provided the Kaashegate with a great supply of distinguished generals.

Effect: Army leader manoeuvre: +1.

Idea 2: The Spirit Desert

The part of Shuvüüshudi we occupy is often called “The Spirit Desert”. Outside Khaashalg, it is the one place in Gozengun where one might travel for days without encountering a single trace of a spirit. The general famine of chi combined with the lack of any landmarks or sites of significance make it impossible for spirits to anchor anywhere, with those that are pushed into the desert by Facestealers very rapidly losing their essence and dissipating.

Effect: Attrition for enemies: +100%.

Idea 3: True to Tradition

On a surface level to an outsider, our Death-Priests and their way of dealing with spirits might resemble the Oni of the demon hills and other practicioners of the Devouring Path, but this assumption is miles away from the truth. Our faith isn’t one of exploitation and our people do not yearn for ever more spiritual power. We are not evil chi-stealers. They couldn’t be more wrong. Our Shamans serve the Supreme Spirit directly and indirectly through the Shepherd of Souls. Our black-masked priests might wield the power to conduct spiritual warfare, but they exercise it in order to protect the ignorant souls from what lies further north. If only they knew…

Effect: Missionary maintenance cost: -20%.

Idea 4: Last Izhuun to Kneel

Despite the proximity to Bhengudak’s staging ground of his reunification of the terror-bird riders, Baohu ak-Ashag, then ruler of the Ashag Kuulgo, was the last Izhuun to accept him as undisputed ruler of the steppe. After Bhengudak’s initial victories, Baohu declared his independence from the ak-Altan Izhuun and gathered his extended family and their bannermen, marching to meet Bhengudak in open battle as he was returning from his southern campaigns subjugating the other Izhuuns.

Baohu, however, seeing the rest of the Shuvüüsh unified and marching east, started envisioning a great new era that the steppe was about to usher in. A new era of unity and prosperity for the Shuvüüsh, something not seen for a very long time. Something he had never seen in his lifetime. Realizing that, he gave an inspiring speech to his gathered host and rode alone to meet Bhengudak and his great army, pledging the Ashag Kuulgo to his cause.

Effect: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.2; Horde unity: +1.

Idea 5: Survival of the Fittest

Life in Shuvüüshudi is not easy by any means. People do not struggle to succeed or prosper, they struggle to survive. During the Husuusing, after the events of the Day of Ashen Skies, our people had to wander the desert with little to no sustenance, under constant threat by wandering rogue spirits, and needing to deal with petty squabbles between themselves. During those times, after the livestock and horses perished, most people followed, with very few surviving and adapting, adapting to the new climate and adopting the terror-birds as their trusted companions. We are descended from those strong few who made it out of the Husuusing period alive, and in our corner of the vast steppe, only the strong will keep surviving.

Effect: Manpower recovery speed: +10%.

Idea 6: Northern Connections

Our lands are situated at the border between the Shuvüüshudi steppe and the northern forests that the Moduk and Khudi peoples call home. Their lands are harsh and unsuitable for our ways of war and they provide resources that are impossible to find in the vast steppe. Instead of struggling for meager plunder from border villages we maintain good trading relations with them, allowing us to enjoy timber and other goods in exchange for grain gathered in the southern spirit-farms.

Effect: Trade efficiency: +10%.

Idea 7: The Burnt Gate

Baohu of Clan Hoifa played a vital role in the initial Shuvüüsh conquest of Gowon. A siege expert, his machinations were put to use in the siege of Onman, whose palace up till then was said to be impregnable. For this he was given the moniker "The Burnt Gate", in the Shuvüüsh tongue "Ashag Kuulgo", a name he would lend to the clan he founded.

Legend says that Bhengudak himself arrived to negotiate the surrender of the king of Danggun, only to find the city sacked and its walls utterly destroyed. Only a lone gate was left standing, its wooden platform burning and its stones blackened. Baohu had made sure the Great Bhengudak wouldn’t need to waste his time with words.

Effect: Siege ability: +25%.

Ambition: Ashag Kuulgo Ambition

Effect: Province warscore cost: -10%.

Rüng Igedch (Y92) — Rüng Igedch Ideas

Traditions: Rüng Igedch Traditions

Effect: Cavalry cost: -15%; same-religion advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Winter Pastures

Our position in the furthest northern reaches of the Shuvüüshudi means that we inhabit large swathes of land that freezes during the winter months. That would be a definite disadvantage was it not for our peoples’ trusted companions, the terror-birds. These creatures are adapted to grazing and sustaining themselves in frozen steppe climates, making our lands ideal for them during the winter months. Any Yomod Rüsh families that respect themselves bring their herds here to graze, come winter time.

Effect: Manpower from true faith provinces: +10%.

Idea 2: The Manticore Banner

The Rüng Igedch is a unique clan, if you can even call them a clan. They were formed out of the 4th great Uvaadum that sported the banner of the Manticore. The clan’s name is relatively new, their leader up until the late 14th century still referred to as commander. Known for its relentlessness and brutality, the 4th Uvaadum saw most of the action in northern Gowon, earning the ire of the local populace. Their atrocities committed during Bhengudak’s early campaigns are still scaring the populace, while their more recent harsh treatment of the Guwaadün in the eastern Shuvüüshudi is still fresh in everyone’s memory. Hopefully, the tradition of wearing Tsagaan the Wise’s great mask will temper the manticore’s rage.

Effect: Morale damage: +10%.

Idea 3: The Maneater Clan

Rüng Igedch, “the maneater clan”, takes its name from the ruthlessness of its leaders. Resembling more a mercenary company than a traditional Shuvüüsh clan, the Rüng Igedch clan head position, if you can even call them that, is not hereditary. The various leading families vy for control of the organisation, each member trying to prove their merit through military might and displays of brutality, hoping that one day they can make a successful power play for the leader’s spot. The scheming and behind the scenes intrigue that accompanies this quasi-stratocratic form of government is what drives the Rüng Igedch to brutality and this very brutality played a critical role in the new-found clan’s name.

Effect: Harsh treatment cost: -25%.

Idea 4: Tsagaan's Wisdom

Tsagaan, the middle brother, was the first to successfully combat a Facestealer and pave the way for our people to be able to follow in his footsteps. Being blessed by the Shepherd of Souls himself, he was able to excorsize the creature using a bundle of juniper. Observing the beast’s inability to find purchase on his brother’s face due to the faceless mask he had on, he propagated the importance of the wooden masks to our ancestors. Tsagaan laid the foundations for how the Saanorgegh operates, and so we honour his wisdom and piety, for he shall forever have our gratitude, saving us from the Facestealer menace. A death priest himself, he is the example for every black-masked shaman, and an exemplar for our Izhuuns past and present.

Effect: Diplomatic advisor cost: -20%.

Idea 5: Southern Diplomacy

The Igedch homeland is far from the warm southern lands of the Kuuldaar where the traditional bonfires that hatch the terror-bird “dragon eggs” take place in the summer. While we rely on terror-birds less than our western cousins, they still form an important part of our society and their use in battle is crucial in projecting our power. Thus, it is necessary to maintain good relations with our southern kin, to make our Yomod Rüsh families’ time in the south more agreeable.

Effect: Stability cost modifier: -15%.

Idea 6: Exploiting Troll Rivalries

The Hill Trolls to the north are not a single political entity. While leaders may rarely arise amongst them and briefly unify their lot, their tenure is usually short lived. They mostly squabble between themselves, thus giving us ideal opportunities to exploit this constant strife for our benefit. Offering our mercenary services to them in exchange for hard labour and northern timber yields great benefits to our people.

Effect: Build cost: -10%.

Idea 7: Dreams of Grandeur

Despite the clan’s controversial roots and the horrendous reputation it accumulated due to transgressions committed during its infancy, it has managed to solidify its hold in the rich lands of the eastern Shuvüüshudi. Well, rich by the standards of the harsh steppe that is. Tsagaan’s guidance has surely done a great amount of work in steering the clan’s leadership towards its current state. Having survived for half a millennium, through Oinukhudi invasions and Gowon retaliations alike, the clan is finally at a position to strike in every direction. Civil strife in the north, imminent rebellion in the east, and a divided warring steppe to the south, makes for the perfect opportunity for the Manticore banner to fly over more and more lands.
